chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ali ibn Khalid al-Maraghi reported to me, saying: Abul Qasim al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Marwan al-Ghazzal narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Hasan al-Ahmasi narrated to us, saying: Khalid ibn Abdillah narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal, who said: I heard Sa'd ibn Malik, meaning Ibn Abi Waqqas, saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, say:
"Fatimah is a part of me; whoever pleases her has pleased me, and whoever displeases her has displeased me. Fatimah is the dearest of all beings to me."

key_terms.البرية: All of creation, all beings — emphasizing Fatimah's supremacy in the Prophet's affection
key_terms.بضعة: A part, a piece of flesh — used to express the closest possible biological and spiritual bond

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about Fatimah being a part of him?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) declared that Fatimah al-Zahra (AS) is a part of him, and that whoever brings her joy has brought joy to him, while whoever causes her harm has harmed him. This hadith, narrated through Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, one of the prominent early companions, establishes the exalted and inviolable status of Fatimah (AS) in the Prophet's household. It was understood by the early Muslim community as a firm prohibition against causing any harm or displeasure to Fatimah, making her contentment inseparable from the Prophet's own.
